title: Impact of NAFTA Tariff Removal on Bilateral Trade Flows

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID)**

This is a classic DID setup. We have:
- **Treatment group**: Country pairs affected by NAFTA tariff removal (treated = 1)
- **Control group**: Country pairs not affected by NAFTA (treated = 0)
- **Pre/Post periods**: Before and after NAFTA implementation (post = 0/1)
- **Interaction term**: treat_x_post captures the causal effect of tariff removal

**Key Assumptions:**
1. **Parallel trends**: Absent NAFTA, trade flows for treated and control country pairs would have followed parallel trajectories over time.
2. **No spillovers (SUTVA)**: NAFTA's tariff removal did not significantly alter trade flows for non-member country pairs (no trade diversion contaminating the control group).
3. **No confounders**: No other policy changes occurred simultaneously that differentially affected NAFTA vs. non-NAFTA pairs.

The DID estimator isolates the NAFTA effect by differencing out time-invariant unobserved heterogeneity across country pairs and common time shocks.

## 2. R Code

```r
# ============================================================
# DID Analysis: Impact of NAFTA Tariff Removal on Trade Flows
# ============================================================

library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)
library(fixest)

# Load data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s44_data.csv")

cat("====== DATA EXPLORATION ======\n")
cat("Dimensions:", dim(df), "\n")
str(df)
summary(df)

# Check panel structure
cat("\nUnique units:", length(unique(df$unit_id)), "\n")
cat("Unique periods:", sort(unique(df$period)), "\n")
cat("Treatment distribution:\n")
print(table(Treated = df$treated, Post = df$post))

# Group means
cat("\n====== GROUP MEANS ======\n")
group_means <- aggregate(y ~ treated + post, data = df, FUN = mean)
print(group_means)

# Manual DID calculation
y_00 <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 0 & df$post == 0])
y_01 <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 0 & df$post == 1])
y_10 <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 1 & df$post == 0])
y_11 <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 1 & df$post == 1])

did_manual <- (y_11 - y_10) - (y_01 - y_00)
cat("\nManual DID estimate:", round(did_manual, 4), "\n")
cat("  Treated pre-mean:  ", round(y_10, 4), "\n")
cat("  Treated post-mean: ", round(y_11, 4), "\n")
cat("  Control pre-mean:  ", round(y_00, 4), "\n")
cat("  Control post-mean: ", round(y_01, 4), "\n")

# ============================================================
# Model 1: Basic DID regression (OLS)
# ============================================================
cat("\n====== MODEL 1: BASIC DID (OLS) ======\n")
model1 <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = df)
summary(model1)

# Robust standard errors
cat("\nWith robust (HC1) standard errors:\n")
robust_se <- coeftest(model1, vcov = vcovHC(model1, type = "HC1"))
print(robust_se)

# ============================================================
# Model 2: DID with unit fixed effects (using fixest)
# ============================================================
cat("\n====== MODEL 2: DID WITH UNIT FIXED EFFECTS ======\n")
model2 <- feols(y ~ post + treat_x_post | unit_id, data = df)
summary(model2)

# ============================================================
# Model 3: DID with unit and period fixed effects (two-way FE)
# ============================================================
cat("\n====== MODEL 3: TWO-WAY FIXED EFFECTS ======\n")
model3 <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = df)
summary(model3)

# ============================================================
# Clustered standard errors at unit level
# ============================================================
cat("\n====== MODEL 1 WITH CLUSTERED SE (unit level) ======\n")
model1_cl <- feols(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, 
                    data = df, cluster = ~unit_id)
summary(model1_cl)

# ============================================================
# ROBUSTNESS CHECKS
# ============================================================
cat("\n====== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ======\n")

# Check 1: Pre-treatment parallel trends (if multiple pre-periods exist)
pre_data <- df[df$post == 0, ]
if (length(unique(pre_data$period)) > 1) {
  cat("\nPre-trend test (treatment x period interaction in pre-period):\n")
  pre_trend_model <- lm(y ~ treated * factor(period), data = pre_data)
  print(summary(pre_trend_model))
} else {
  cat("\nOnly one pre-period available; formal pre-trend test not feasible.\n")
  cat("Comparing pre-period distributions:\n")
  cat("  Treated pre-period mean:", round(mean(pre_data$y[pre_data$treated == 1]), 4), "\n")
  cat("  Control pre-period mean:", round(mean(pre_data$y[pre_data$treated == 0]), 4), "\n")
  t_test_pre <- t.test(y ~ treated, data = pre_data)
  cat("  Pre-period t-test p-value:", round(t_test_pre$p.value, 4), "\n")
}

# Check 2: Placebo test - assign fake treatment to control group
cat("\nPlacebo test (random treatment among control units):\n")
set.seed(42)
control_data <- df[df$treated == 0, ]
control_units <- unique(control_data$unit_id)
placebo_treated <- sample(control_units, length(control_units) / 2)
control_data$placebo_treat <- as.integer(control_data$unit_id %in% placebo_treated)
control_data$placebo_interact <- control_data$placebo_treat * control_data$post
placebo_model <- lm(y ~ placebo_treat + post + placebo_interact, data = control_data)
cat("Placebo DID coefficient:", round(coef(placebo_model)["placebo_interact"], 4), "\n")
cat("Placebo p-value:", round(summary(placebo_model)$coefficients["placebo_interact", 4], 4), "\n")

# Check 3: Quantile effects (median regression)
cat("\nMedian regression (quantile = 0.5):\n")
library(quantreg)
qr_model <- rq(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = df, tau = 0.5)
print(summary(qr_model))

# ============================================================
# SUMMARY OF RESULTS
# ============================================================
cat("\n====== SUMMARY OF KEY RESULTS ======\n")
cat("==============================================\n")
cat(sprintf("DID Estimate (OLS):           %.4f (SE: %.4f, p: %.4f)\n",
            coef(model1)["treat_x_post"],
            summary(model1)$coefficients["treat_x_post", 2],
            summary(model1)$coefficients["treat_x_post", 4]))
cat(sprintf("DID Estimate (Robust SE):     %.4f (SE: %.4f, p: %.4f)\n",
            robust_se["treat_x_post", 1],
            robust_se["treat_x_post", 2],
            robust_se["treat_x_post", 4]))
cat(sprintf("DID Estimate (Unit FE):       %.4f\n",
            coef(model2)["treat_x_post"]))
cat(sprintf("DID Estimate (Two-way FE):    %.4f\n",
            coef(model3)["treat_x_post"]))
cat("==============================================\n")

# Interpretation
did_coef <- coef(model1)["treat_x_post"]
cat(sprintf("\nInterpretation: NAFTA tariff removal is associated with a %.1f%% \n", 
            (exp(did_coef) - 1) * 100))
cat("change in bilateral trade flows between member countries.\n")
cat(sprintf("(In log points: %.4f)\n", did_coef))
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Expected Sign:** **Positive**. The removal of tariffs under NAFTA should increase bilateral trade flows between member countries. This is the standard prediction from trade theory — reducing trade barriers lowers the cost of cross-border transactions, leading to trade creation.

**Expected Magnitude:** Given that the outcome is log bilateral trade flows, I expect the DID coefficient (treat_x_post) to be in the range of **0.3 to 1.5 log points**, corresponding to roughly a **35% to 350% increase** in trade flows. The gravity model literature on NAFTA typically finds effects in the range of 0.3–0.6 log points for the early years, though simulated data may show a stronger/cleaner effect.

**Robustness expectations:**
- The coefficient should be **statistically significant** across all specifications (OLS, robust SE, unit FE, two-way FE).
- The **placebo test** should yield an insignificant coefficient, confirming the effect is specific to NAFTA-treated pairs.
- Pre-period balance checks should show no significant pre-existing differences in trends between treated and control groups, validating the parallel trends assumption.
- Results should be stable across specifications, with unit fixed effects potentially improving precision by absorbing pair-specific heterogeneity.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Comparing trade flows before and after NAFTA for treated and control pairs.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The tariff removal under NAFTA led to a significant increase in bilateral trade flows.
